response: Yes, patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) after aortic valve replacement can affect survival and quality of life in elderly patients. PPM occurs when the implanted prosthetic valve is too small for the patient's body size, leading to inefficient blood flow and increased energy expenditure by the heart. This can result in decreased exercise tolerance, increased symptoms, and reduced long-term survival. Elderly patients with PPM may experience a decline in their physical function, reduced ability to perform daily activities, and a decreased overall quality of life. Therefore, it is essential to carefully select the appropriate prosthetic valve size during aortic valve replacement surgery to minimize the risk of PPM and optimize outcomes in elderly patients.
